input.quote: ARTICLE XII INDEMNITY Licensee will be solely responsible for any commercial or legal liability that may arise as a result of Licensee's exercise of any of the license rights granted by Licensor to Licensee under this Agreement, and Licensee shall defend, indemnify, and hold Licensor harmless from and against any and all suits, claims, proceedings, judgments, awards, damages, loss, liability, cost and expenses
input.rationale: Article XII is a one-way indemnity: only Licensee (our party) defends and indemnifies Licensor, and its triggers are extremely broad (any exercise of the licence, the conduct of Licensee's business, and any breach of any term). There is no Licensor indemnity anywhere in the Agreement — the only other "indemnity" reference (p0127) concerns bonds for injunctive relief. Worse, Article XIII(a) affirmatively disclaims all Licensor liability for claims that use of the Licensed Technology infringes third-party intellectual property rights, and Article XIII(b) caps Licensor's total liability at one half of amounts paid, while the warranty disclaimer (sec-p0109/p0112) disclaims non-infringement. This is the playbook walk-away scenario (no Vendor IP indemnity plus a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's technology). The redline adds a Licensor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation, breach of law, unauthorised access to Licensee data, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure and an express carve-out from the Article XIII exclusions and cap (otherwise the indemnity would be nullified by the IP disclaimer). It also narrows our own indemnity to Licensee-provided content and our breach of applicable law, per the preferred position.

proposal.summary: Add Licensor IP/misconduct indemnity in Article XII and narrow Licensee's indemnity to Licensee content and breach of law
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article XII is a one-way indemnity running only to Licensor, and Article XIII expressly disclaims any Licensor liability for infringement claims, so we have no protection if the Licensed Technology infringes a third party's IP. We have added a reciprocal Licensor defence and indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct (carved out of the Article XIII exclusions and cap), and narrowed our own indemnity to Licensee-provided content and our breach of law. If helpful, we can discuss the usual IP indemnity exclusions (our modifications, combinations, specifications) and a super-cap of 3x annual fees as a fallback.

In each case, the indemnified party shall give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of the claim, the indemnifying party shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim (provided that no settlement imposing any liability or obligation on, or requiring any admission by, the indemnified party shall be made without its prior written consent), and the indemnified party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.
